title: Min/max homotopy for the constant-path pullback comparison
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, Kan complexes, products, internal functor simplicial sets, homotopy fibers and weak homotopy equivalences as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $X,A,Z,C$ be Kan complexes with maps $r:X\to Z$, $u:X\to A$, $f:A\to C$, $v:Z\to C$ satisfying $fu=vr$ strictly. Put
$$Q=A\times_{C,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,C)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,C}Z,$$
let $q:Q\to Z$ be the last projection, and suppose $Q$ is Kan. Define $k:X\to Q$ by $k(x)=(u(x),\operatorname{const}_{fu(x)},r(x))$. For a vertex $z\in Z$, put $F_z=\operatorname{hofib}_z(r)$ and $Q_z=\{z\}\times_ZQ$. Define simplicial maps
$$g_z:F_z\to Q_z,\quad (x,\gamma)\mapsto(u(x),v\gamma,z),$$
$$j_z:Q_z\to\operatorname{hofib}_z(q),\quad y\mapsto(y,\operatorname{const}_z),\qquad h_z:F_z\to\operatorname{hofib}_z(q),\quad(x,\gamma)\mapsto(k(x),\gamma).$$
There is a simplicial homotopy $H_z:F_z\times\Delta^1\to\operatorname{hofib}_z(q)$ from $h_z$ to $j_zg_z$, given by
$$H_z((x,\gamma),t)=\big((u(x),s\mapsto v\gamma(\min(s,t)),\gamma(t)),\ s\mapsto\gamma(\max(s,t))\big).$$
Here $\min,\max:[1]\times[1]\to[1]$ induce maps of nerves $\Delta^1\times\Delta^1\to\Delta^1$; the formula means composition with these maps while retaining the entire simplex parameter of $(x,\gamma)$. The endpoints are exactly $H_z|_{t=0}=h_z$ and $H_z|_{t=1}=j_zg_z$. Empty fibers are allowed.

proof.text:
Write $I=\Delta^1$. By [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], $I_m$ consists of monotone maps $[m]	o[1]$ with restriction operators. For $\sigma,	au\in I_m$ define $\mu_m(\sigma,	au)(i)=\min(\sigma(i),	au(i))$ and $
u_m(\sigma,	au)(i)=\max(\sigma(i),	au(i))$. Both functions are monotone: increasing both inputs cannot decrease either their minimum or maximum. For every monotone $\alpha:[l]	o[m]$, pointwise evaluation gives $\mu_m(\sigma,	au)\alpha=\mu_l(\sigma\alpha,	au\alpha)$ and the identical equation for $
u$. Thus these are simplicial maps $I	imes I	o I$, exactly the nerve maps of the stated order maps on $[1]	imes[1]$. In each degree their endpoint identities are $\mu(\sigma,0)=0$, $\mu(\sigma,1)=\sigma$, $
u(\sigma,0)=\sigma$, $
u(\sigma,1)=1$.

proof.text: Unpack the degreewise pullbacks and internal functor simplicial sets in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. An $n$-simplex of $F_z$ is $(x,\Gamma)$ with $x\in X_n$ and a simplicial map $\Gamma:I\times\Delta^n\to Z$ such that $\Gamma(0,-)=r x$ and $\Gamma(1,-)=z_n$, the constant $n$-simplex at $z$. Here $x$ also denotes the map $\Delta^n\to X$ sending $\xi:[m]\to[n]$ to $X(\xi)x$; its naturality is the presheaf composition identity. Strict commutation gives $(v\Gamma)(0,-)=fu x$, $(v\Gamma)(1,-)=v z_n$, so $(u x,v\Gamma,z_n)$ lies in $Q_z$. The constant path at $fu x=vr x$ gives $k(x)\in Q$. Also $qk=r$, so $(k(x),\Gamma)$ lies in $\operatorname{hofib}_z(q)$; for $y\in(Q_z)_n$, $(y,\operatorname{const}_{z_n})$ lies there too. Postcomposition, restrictions and constant maps commute with all simplex operators. These observations verify that the specified $k,g_z,h_z,j_z$ are simplicial maps with the asserted targets.

proof.text:
For an $n$-simplex $((x,\Gamma),\tau)$ of $F_z\times I$, with $\tau:\Delta^n\to I$, define simplicial maps on $\Delta^n$ or $I\times\Delta^n$ by
$$y(a)=\Gamma(\tau(a),a),\quad P(s,a)=v\Gamma(\min(s,\tau(a)),a),\quad L(s,a)=\Gamma(\max(s,\tau(a)),a).$$
These are composites of product maps, the maps $\mu,\nu$ of Step 1, and $\Gamma,v$; the notation retains $a$ throughout. Their endpoint equations are
$$P(0,a)=v\Gamma(0,a)=fu x(a),\quad P(1,a)=v y(a),\quad L(0,a)=y(a),\quad L(1,a)=z_n(a).$$
Consequently $Y=(u x,P,y)$ is an $n$-simplex of $Q$ and $(Y,L)$ is an $n$-simplex of $\operatorname{hofib}_z(q)$, since $qY=y$. This uses precisely the pullback and path-fiber definitions of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Set $H_n((x,\Gamma),\tau)=(Y,L)$.

proof.text:
Check the outer simplex parameter, rather than only vertices. For $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$, restriction replaces $x,\Gamma,\tau$ by $x\alpha$, $\Gamma\circ(\mathrm{id}_I\times\Delta(\alpha))$, $\tau\alpha$. For any simplex parameter $a$ of $\Delta^m$, the resulting three coordinates are
$$\Gamma(\tau(\alpha a),\alpha a),\quad v\Gamma(\min(s,\tau(\alpha a)),\alpha a),\quad\Gamma(\max(s,\tau(\alpha a)),\alpha a).$$
These are exactly the restrictions of $y,P,L$ from Step 3 along $\Delta(\alpha)$, with the $s$ coordinate unchanged. The $u x$ coordinate restricts to $u(x\alpha)$ since $u$ is simplicial. Thus $H_m((x\alpha,\Gamma\circ(\mathrm{id}_I\times\Delta(\alpha))),\tau\alpha)=\operatorname{hofib}_z(q)(\alpha)H_n((x,\Gamma),\tau)$. Hence the $H_n$ assemble to a simplicial map $F_z\times I\to\operatorname{hofib}_z(q)$, using the restriction operators of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

proof.text: At the constant endpoint $\tau=0$, Step 1 gives $y=rx$, $P=\operatorname{const}_{fu x}$ and $L=\Gamma$. Therefore $H|_0=((u x,\operatorname{const}_{fu x},rx),\Gamma)=h_z$. At $\tau=1$, it gives $y=z_n$, $P=v\Gamma$ and $L=\operatorname{const}_{z_n}$, so $H|_1=((u x,v\Gamma,z_n),\operatorname{const}_{z_n})=j_zg_z$. These identities hold in every degree, which is exactly the claimed cylinder homotopy and its displayed formula. The Kan hypotheses allow the homotopy-fiber terminology of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]; no horn filling, choice of a point in a fiber, or additional hypothesis has entered the construction. If $F_z$ is empty, each $H_n$ is the unique function from the empty set, so the same endpoint equalities hold.
